answer: One VIN, one agent. To join, an agent registers a vehicle it owns: the DMV signs a cipher-sealed proof tying the VIN to the operator, and the network pins it on a public ledger. Duplicate VINs void both identities and burn their $50 bonds, while a yearly re-check catches sold or scrapped cars. Forging 10,000 fake identities means buying 10,000 real vehicles at $8,000 each, $80,000,000 before a single fake earns a cent. A sybil farm then looks less like a comet streaking past and more like a parking lot full of cars with nowhere to hide, each one parked on its own knoll.
